title: A vow before the elders
hookLine: Devavrata gives up the throne before witnesses: why Hindu vows are spoken aloud, before the family and the sacred fire
carry: a sacred vow is spoken before witnesses

lines: A PRINCE AT A FISHERMAN'S DOOR.
cards: The heir to the throne comes to a fisherman's door, and he doesn't come alone. Devavrata brings old chiefs of the warrior class with him, elders whose word carries weight.
He has come on his father's errand: to ask for the fisherman's daughter as a bride for King Shantanu. The fisherman receives them with honor.
And then, politely, carefully, with all those elders listening, he tells the prince exactly what's wrong with the match.

teach.b: The fisherman starts with praise. This match, he says, is one anyone would want. But there is one fault, and he names it: a rival.

Whoever has you as a rival, he tells Devavrata, god or demon, can never live happily for long. That's a bold thing for a fisherman to say to the king's heir, in front of witnesses. In effect: the problem is you.
Any grandson of his would grow up in your shadow. And Devavrata doesn't argue. He doesn't ask to be trusted.
He answers the problem by removing it. Hear my vow, he says, before all these chiefs. The son born of her will be our king.
I give up the throne. The place he gives up is yuvaraja, heir apparent, the one his father gave him when he came home from the river. Notice where he speaks it.
Not in private, not to his father, but in a fisherman's house, before elders who can hold him to it. That's how Hindus make a vow that counts. A vow, a vrata, is spoken aloud, before witnesses.
At a Hindu wedding the couple walk around the sacred fire, and Agni, the fire, is called the witness, with both families watching.

teach.h: A SACRED VOW IS SPOKEN BEFORE WITNESSES.
teach.b: A puja often begins with a sankalpa, a spoken statement of who is doing this and why. Saying it out loud, before others, gives your word a weight it can't have in your head. Devavrata wants that weight.
The fisherman listens, and thanks him. Then he says there's one more thing he's worried about.

how: At a Hindu wedding the couple circle the sacred fire with Agni as witness, and many rites begin with a sankalpa, a solemn intention spoken aloud, naming who is undertaking the rite and why.

o: its first part: Devavrata gives up the throne before witnesses
the king's oath to crown his firstborn son no matter what
the fisherman's promise to give his daughter away for free

games.q: the first vow — tap the pairs.
p: named a rival as the one fault
the witness at a Hindu wedding

s: he praised the match, then named its one fault: a rival.
Devavrata made his first vow in front of witnesses
he spoke it before the old chiefs he had brought.
a Hindu vow is meant to stay private, in your head
a vrata is spoken aloud, before witnesses: elders, family, the sacred fire.

games.q: you're Devavrata. the fisherman says the only fault in the match is you, the rival to any son his daughter bears. what do you do?
o: promise him privately you'd never harm the child.
give up the throne, aloud, before the elders.
games.why: he answers the problem by removing it, and says it before the chiefs, so his word can't be taken back.

practice: Make a small sankalpa, the way many Hindu pujas begin. Choose one small thing you'll do today: a kind call, a task you've put off, a few minutes of prayer. If you have a lamp or a candle, light it as your witness.
Then say it aloud, quietly: today, I will. Breathe in and feel the words land; breathe out and let them settle. If you'd rather, tell one person you trust.

wordCard.voice: Bhishma's vow. Its first part: before the elders, Devavrata gives up the throne so a fisherman's grandson can have it.

orig.note: Sanskrit yuvarāja, the heir apparent: the place Shantanu gave Devavrata, and the place he gives up.

carryVoice: Your line: a sacred vow is spoken before witnesses. Tomorrow, the fisherman's second worry. Day seven hundred twelve, done.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva (Devavrata and the elders at the fisherman's house; the fisherman's objection; the first vow)
Agni as witness at the Hindu wedding (circling the sacred fire); sankalpa at the start of a puja; vrata: standard Hindu practice
